vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[Django](https://pypi.org/project/Django/) is a high-level Python Web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to SQL Injection via the band index parameter `band_lhs` in `check_raster` lookups when using PostGIS. An attacker can execute arbitrary SQL commands by supplying crafted input to this parameter.
## Remediation
Upgrade `Django` to version 4.2.28, 5.2.11, 6.0.2 or higher.
## References
- [Django Release Notes](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/security/#CVE-2026-1207)
- [Django Security Release](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/feb/03/security-releases/#CVE-2026-1207)
- [GitHub Advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mwm9-4648-f68q)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/django/django/commit/17a1d64a58ef24c0c3b78d66d86f5415075f18f0)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/django/django/commit/8f77e7301174834573614ae90e1826fdf27f8a24)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/django/django/commit/a14363102d98fa29b8cced578eb3a0fadaa5bcb7)
- [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/django-announce#CVE-2026-1207)
- [Nuclei Templates](https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates/blob/main/http/cves/2026/CVE-2026-1207.yaml)

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[Django](https://pypi.org/project/Django/) is a high-level Python Web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Missing Authorization in the admin changelist forms using `ModelAdmin.list_editable`. An attacker can gain unauthorized access to create new instances by submitting forged `POST` data.
## Remediation
Upgrade `Django` to version 4.2.30, 5.2.13, 6.0.4 or higher.
## References
- [Django Release Notes](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/security/)
- [Django Security Release](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/apr/07/security-releases/)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/django/django/commit/428c48f358c5a0ed5ca2834fb721d615eb2b0e11)

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[Django](https://pypi.org/project/Django/) is a high-level Python Web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the ASGI requests with a missing or understated `Content-Length` header when reading `HttpRequest.body`. An attacker can exhaust system memory by sending a specially crafted request that bypasses the intended memory upload limit.
## Remediation
Upgrade `Django` to version 4.2.30, 5.2.13, 6.0.4 or higher.
## References
- [Django Release Notes](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/security/)
- [Django Security Release](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/apr/07/security-releases/)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/django/django/commit/393dbc53e848876fdba92fbf02e10ee6a6eace6b)

vulnerabilities.title: Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[Django](https://pypi.org/project/Django/) is a high-level Python Web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity in the `MultiPartParser` when handling multipart uploads with `Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64` containing excessive whitespace. An attacker can cause significant resource consumption and degrade server performance by submitting specially crafted file uploads.
## Remediation
Upgrade `Django` to version 4.2.30, 5.2.13, 6.0.4 or higher.
## References
- [Django Release Notes](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/security/)
- [Django Security Release](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/apr/07/security-releases/)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/django/django/commit/0910af60468216c856dfbcac1177372c225deb76)

vulnerabilities.title: User Impersonation
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[Django](https://pypi.org/project/Django/) is a high-level Python Web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to User Impersonation via the `ASGIRequest` objects. An attacker can impersonate users or manipulate request headers by exploiting the ambiguous mapping between headers containing hyphens and underscores.
## Remediation
Upgrade `Django` to version 4.2.30, 5.2.13, 6.0.4 or higher.
## References
- [Django Release Notes](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/security/)
- [Django Security Release](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/apr/07/security-releases/)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/django/django/commit/a623c3982857e80324448f85c7faf9a6710330ef)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity due to improper handling of `Cache-Control` directives in `UpdateCacheMiddleware`. An attacker can gain unauthorized access to sensitive response data by sending requests with uppercase or mixed-case `Cache-Control` values, causing private data to be cached and subsequently served to other users.
## Remediation
Upgrade `django` to version 5.2.15, 6.0.6 or higher.
## References
- [Django Release Notes](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/security/)
- [Django Security Release](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/jun/03/security-releases/)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/django/django/commit/b4330259ffbe1a031ed14daab1f35697460f10f2)
- [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/django-announce)

vulnerabilities.title: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information in the `EmailBackend` function when a failed `STARTTLS` handshake occurs and `fail_silently=True` is set. An attacker can intercept and read email content by performing a man-in-the-middle attack on the network connection.
## Remediation
Upgrade `django` to version 5.2.15, 6.0.6 or higher.
## References
- [Django Release Notes](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/security/)
- [Django Security Release](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/jun/03/security-releases/)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/django/django/commit/df887f50198593a0e5b4638bfddbbd43a30fd276)
- [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/django-announce)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature in the `get_signed_cookie` function. An attacker can access data intended for a different context by crafting distinct `(name, salt)` pairs that result in the same concatenated value.
## Remediation
Upgrade `django` to version 5.2.15, 6.0.6 or higher.
## References
- [Django Release Notes](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/security/)
- [Django Security Release](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/jun/03/security-releases/)

- [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/django-announce)

vulnerabilities.title: Incomplete Comparison with Missing Factors
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Incomplete Comparison with Missing Factors in the `has_vary_header` function. An attacker can gain access to cached responses intended for other users by sending requests with whitespace-padded `Vary` header values.
## Remediation
Upgrade `django` to version 5.2.15, 6.0.6 or higher.
## References

vulnerabilities.title: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information in the `UpdateCacheMiddleware` function. An attacker can access sensitive cached data by making unauthenticated requests to endpoints that have previously been accessed with an `Authorization` header, due to the absence of the `Authorization` value in the `Vary` response header.
## Remediation
Upgrade `django` to version 5.2.15, 6.0.6 or higher.
## References
- [Django Release Notes](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/dev/releases/security/)
- [Django Security Release](https://www.djangoproject.com/weblog/2026/jun/03/security-releases/)
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/django/django/commit/a2faa8e895926ac5d63f72879b5ccf671b5b4ba9)
- [Google Groups Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/django-announce)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Neutralization
vulnerabilities.description:

vulnerabilities.title: Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[Django](https://pypi.org/project/Django/) is a high-level Python Web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value in the `GDALRaster` process when constructed from a bytes object. An attacker can access adjacent memory or cause service degradation by accessing the `vsi_buffer` property.

vulnerabilities.title: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[Django](https://pypi.org/project/Django/) is a high-level Python Web framework that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information in the `UpdateCacheMiddleware` and `cache_page` process when responses that vary on cookies are cached while the incoming request contains unrelated cookies. An attacker can access private data from the shared cache by making crafted requests that manipulate cookies.
## Remediation
Upgrade `Django` to version 5.2.16, 6.0.7 or higher.
## References
